claims.text: DFT+U or hybrid functionals can reveal ferromagnetic ground states in transition-metal-based materials when standard DFT fails.
Standard DFT may fail to resolve subtle energy differences between competing spin configurations.
Insufficient treatment of electron correlations by standard DFT can produce ambiguous or non-magnetic ordering.
Spin-polarized DFT+U or hybrid-functional calculations better describe localized d electrons.
Spin-polarized DFT+U or hybrid-functional calculations better describe exchange interactions.
Near-zero-temperature calculations can resolve the energy ordering of ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, and nonmagnetic states.
Electron spin configurations and localized magnetic moments mediate the predicted magnetic ground state.
The Hubbard U term corrects self-interaction errors and underlocalization present in standard DFT.
Exact exchange in hybrid functionals corrects self-interaction errors and underlocalization present in standard DFT.
Correcting self-interaction and underlocalization stabilizes the ferromagnetic state by improving computed energy differences between spin alignments.
A ferromagnetic configuration with lower total energy than all competing magnetic configurations constitutes a computed ferromagnetic ground state.
LDA and GGA are exchange-correlation approximations used in standard DFT calculations.
LDA or GGA may inadequately capture strong electron correlations and therefore give ambiguous or incorrect magnetic ground-state predictions.
The stabilization energy and magnetic-moment enhancement depend on the material system and the selected Hubbard U parameter.
Systems with weak electron correlations may show minimal differences between standard and advanced DFT treatments.
Quantitative energy differences and magnetic moments depend on computational parameters and the material system.
Failure of DFT+U or hybrid functionals to lower the ferromagnetic state's energy relative to competing states would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to significantly enhance magnetic moments relative to standard DFT would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis is defined by a lower ferromagnetic total energy, but the falsification rule additionally treats lack of significantly enhanced magnetic moments as independently decisive. A method could predict a lower-energy ferromagnetic state without enhancing the moment, so this added criterion is not logically required by the stated hypothesis.
